Let's use integration by parts. We set

$$
\begin{aligned}u=2x & ⇒ & {u}^{′}=2 \\ {v}^{′}={e}^{x} & ⇒ & v={e}^{x}.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting the above into the integration by parts formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\ \int 2x\cdot {e}^{x}\,\text{d}x & =2x\cdot {e}^{x}-\int {e}^{x}\cdot 2\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate the integral and get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}2x{e}^{x}\,\text{d}x & =2x{e}^{x}\,{|}_{0}^{1}-2{\int }_{0}^{1}{e}^{x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =2x{e}^{x}\,{|}_{0}^{1}-2{e}^{x}\,{|}_{0}^{1} \\  & =2(1\cdot {e}^{1}-0\cdot {e}^{0})-2({e}^{1}-{e}^{0}) \\  & =2e-2(e-1) \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$
